messages:
marta: Hey folks — after upgrading the ruby-ffi native extension to 0.9.1, our minimal sampleapp shows steady memory growth under embed-heavy load. Not sure if it's GC related or a native leak. Anyone seen this?

alex: Not on my end yet. Can you paste a tiny repro or heap stats?

marta: Quick repro steps: run scripts/sample_embed_runner.sh with EMBED_COUNT=2000. Memory climbs ~10MB/min. Attached a short trace:
```
# simplified loop
1000.times do
  embeddings = client.embeddings(input: "x" * 1024)
end
```
I also dumped object space and saw many native pointers still live.

sam: Ok that rings a bell. We changed how we store a pointer to the Ruby String in the C struct in 0.9.1 to avoid copying. But we didn't register it with the GC (rb_gc_mark) so GC moves/free can confuse the C layer. Likely root cause.

jamie: Oof. That explains it. Simple repro, thanks. If that's the case the fix is to RB_OBJ_WRITE or mark the value so GC knows about it. I'll take the PR review.

marta: Thanks — I put up a quick PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-ffi/pull/456 — fixes storage to use rb_gc_register_address + added a stress test (50k iterations). Also added a tiny CI job that runs the sampleapp for 30s.

alex: Nice. I ran the branch locally — memory stabilizes now in my runs. Two small nits inline on the PR but nothing blocking.

jamie: Reviewing now. Can we also add a comment referencing the original commit that introduced the change? Will make future bisects easier.

sam: Agreed. Add a changelog note too (bugfix, ffi). After that I can merge and cut a patch release (0.9.1 -> 0.9.2).

marta: Added commit with comment + changelog entry. Thanks all. :tada:

deploy-bot: deploy-queue: patch-release/0.9.2 queued to staging (artifact: ruby-ffi-0.9.2.gem). ETA ~12m.

alex: I'll smoke test staging against sampleapp after deploy.

marta: Appreciate it. If anyone sees regressions ping me here.

jamie: LGTM — marking reviewed and assigning sam for final merge.

sam: Merged and published 0.9.2. Closing the PR. Thanks everyone for quick turnaround.

marta: Verified in our staging harness — no more memory creep. Closing the loop :smile:
